name: Existential & Global Catastrophic Risk
description: Threats that could end or permanently derail civilization: engineered pandemics, nuclear war and nuclear winter, unaligned AI, asteroids and supervolcanoes, societal collapse, and how much to prioritize, slow, or surveil to prevent them.

name: AI & Machine Intelligence
description: How advanced AI is built, governed, and understood: how fast capabilities are growing, how systems are kept aligned with human intent, how labs and governments regulate them, what they cost in energy and data, and whether machine minds could ever matter morally.

name: Digital Society & Information
description: Life inside networked technology: online speech and moderation, privacy and surveillance, who owns data, encryption, automated decisions, and how deepfakes and algorithms shape what a society believes.

name: Climate & Energy
description: The energy transition and the climate it is racing: which power sources to build, how to price and remove carbon, how fast to phase out fossil fuels, and what to do about tipping points, geoengineering, and the cost of it all.

name: Bio, Health & the Human Body
description: Medicine and biotechnology at the edges of the human body: gene editing and embryo selection, drugs and how they are priced and approved, mental health, aging, reproduction, and the choices around the end of life.

name: Economy & Work
description: How wealth and work are organized: inequality and wages, taxation, trade and industrial policy, housing, public debt, money and its future, the structure of firms and markets, and what automation does to jobs.

name: Governance & Political Order
description: How power is constituted and constrained: democracy and its rivals, elections and courts, executive power, crime and drugs, immigration and borders, war and weapons, and the international order.

name: Society, Culture & Identity
description: How communities and identities are changing: birth rates and family, education, religion, loneliness, identity and belonging, historical injustice, the media people trust, and the institutions that hold a society together.

name: Ethics & Philosophy
description: The foundations under everything else: whether moral facts are real, free will, personal identity, meaning, the moral status of animals and the unborn, and what we owe to strangers and to future generations.

name: Food, Land & the Living World
description: How we feed ourselves and share the planet: farming methods, meat and its alternatives, animal welfare, land and water use, protected areas, wildfire, plastics, and how far to intervene in nature.
